subtitle: A modular drive-train connection
description: Two flanged hubs and a spacer envelope explore a bought flexible element. Tooth forms and elastomer geometry are not designed, so this is not a working gear or flexible coupling.
decisions: Buy the flexible element or full coupling for the first prototypes.
Keep hub removal and brake-disc access visible in the packaging study.
Treat torsional resonance and misalignment separately from static torque.
materials: Hubs: 42CrMo4 candidate, condition to be selected for section and fatigue.
Flexible element: vendor-controlled compound or gear assembly.
risks: No transmitting connection between the placeholder flexible element and hubs is released.
No keyway, shaft fit, balancing or retention design.
steps: Approve shaft and torsional system requirements.
Replace spacer with qualified supplier geometry.
Finalize hub attachment, alignment and guarding before prototype assembly.
validation: Shaft torsion, key/locking connection, fatigue and critical-speed assessment.
Supplier torque/misalignment endurance and balance confirmation.
hypotheses: Hub removal without rotor damage target
Validate on a physical installation mock-up.
Compare quoted full-coupling integration against a custom programme.
sensors: Reserve guard clearance and optional vibration/speed monitoring; no sensors in rotating masses.
